Description: Pellet consumption scores points. When the player moves onto a square containing a pellet, the system shall add the pellet value to the score and remove the pellet. (Source: PlayerCollisions.playerVersusPellet, PointCalculator.consumedAPellet.)

Ghosts do not consume pellets. When a ghost moves onto a square containing a pellet, the system shall keep the pellet on the square and move the ghost to that square without changing the score. (Source: Level.move, Unit.occupy.)

Moving onto an empty square does not change the score. When the player moves onto an accessible empty square, the system shall move the player to that square without changing the score. (Source: Level.move, DefaultPointCalculator.pacmanMoved.)
Walls block movement. When a player attempts to move into a wall, the system shall leave the player in the current square. (Source: Level.move, BoardFactory.Wall.isAccessibleTo.)

Ghost collisions end the game. When a player collides with a ghost, the system shall mark the player as dead and stop the game. (Source: PlayerCollisions.playerVersusGhost, Level.updateObservers, Game.levelLost.)

Eating the last pellet wins the game. When no pellets remain on the board, the system shall declare the level won and stop the game. (Source: Level.remainingPellets, Level.updateObservers, Game.levelWon.)

The level is lost when the player dies. When no players remain alive, the system shall declare the level lost and stop the game. (Source: Level.updateObservers, Level.isAnyPlayerAlive(), Game.levelLost.)

Ghosts move on scheduled turns. While the level is running, the system shall periodically request a move from each ghost and move it when a direction is returned. (Source: Level.startNPCs, Level.NpcMoveTask.run, Ghost.nextMove.)
Player movement requires an active game. When the game is not in progress, the system shall ignore requests to move a player. (Source: Game.move.)

Starting requires a playable level. When a game is started, the system shall start it only if at least one player is alive and at least one pellet remains. (Source: Game.start, Level.isAnyPlayerAlive, Level.remainingPellets.)

Map input is validated. When loading a text map, the system shall reject rows of unequal width and characters that do not represent an empty square, wall, pellet, ghost, or player start. (Source: MapParser.checkMapFormat, MapParser.addSquare.)

Players receive starting positions. When a player is registered for a level for the first time, the system shall place that player on the next starting square, cycling through the available starting squares; repeated registration shall have no effect. (Source: Level.registerPlayer.)
Attempted direction is recorded. When a unit attempts to move, the system shall update its facing direction even if the destination is inaccessible. (Source: Level.move, Unit.setDirection.)

Pausing suspends movement. When the game is stopped, the system shall stop ghost scheduling and reject subsequent player and ghost movement until the game resumes. (Source: Game.stop, Level.stop, Level.move.)

Board edges connect as tunnels. When a player or ghost moves beyond a board edge, the system shall move that unit to the corresponding square on the opposite edge. (Source: BoardFactory.createBoard, Square.getSquareAt, Level.move.)

Usability: Consistent movement directions. The system shall represent movement using exactly four cardinal directions: NORTH, SOUTH, EAST, and WEST, with each direction corresponding to a single grid step. (Source: Direction.NORTH, Direction.SOUTH, Direction.WEST, Direction.EAST, Direction.getDeltaX, Direction.getDeltaY.)
